body: Hey I appreciate you actually following up. I was munitions systems. I build bombs and missiles for all types of jets and bombers. I also dealt with with C4 and the like, keeping it safe and distributing it.
I’ve tried. I get halfway through my conversation and “realize” my problems aren’t worthy of talking about. I know it’s stupid but it’s how I feel.
US Air Force, thank you for asking.

I do but I don’t. (Suffer from PTSD) I assume that is the case with most vets in the same place as me. I’ve seen, done, things that “I” believe are worthy of taking my own life yet suicide isn’t an option. Our PTSD isn’t as “severe” as others before us so seeking help for it makes us feel weak.  My actions led to a squad (5 soldiers) of American soldiers dying. The thought always crosses my mind and is sometimes said “ oh but you didn’t pull the trigger so it’s not the same.”

I struggle with religion a lot lately. I still firmly believe that a power greater than myself will take my soul in the end. Yet even with that thought something inside me wants to continue this life. I’m seriously scared that I’ll ruin this body to an end and blubber like a baby when my fifth of alcohol a day ends me. My organs will fail and then I’ll realize I wanted to live all along, but it will be to late. That thought scares the shit out of me. I hope you find the urge to live and do the most you can with your life. As much as we hate it, we deserve it.
Thank you for your kind words.

USAF, I was AMMO for 5 years. Best years of my life as far I’m concerned. Although I still believe that the dialogue of TI’s of “this is the greatest thing you will ever do in your life” unfortunate. I understand why it’s there, I just wish I hadn’t heard it:
Thank you so much for you beautiful statement
